name: typescript-esm-named-import-proof-v1
meaning: Proof-contract fixtures for the TypeScript relative ESM named-import proof policy v1. Each case marks exactly one call with /* claim */ in its importer file. expected_class is the answer the frozen restricted rule must give (must: exactly one target, the marked exported declaration; unknown: no target). These are NOT independent ground-truth labels and NOT part of docs/dispatch-corpus.json, its 49-case denominator, or any improvement claim. runtime_truth records what Node actually executes where the case is runnable.
analysis_root_rule: Each case directory is analyzed as its own project root; predicted paths use Girder's existing module_path for files relative to that root.

correction: correction-1 (after the high review NO-GO on 79b7e70): adds E3 spelling and encoding refusals, v1 extensions narrowed to .ts/.mts, mock refusal by resolved module identity, canonical identity and symlink cases, mixed-language collision, an unrelated-imports positive control, and an incremental sequence. Entries for the original 40 cases are unchanged. correction-2 (after the second high review NO-GO on 7fdfdd2): HOOK-1..3 refusals and a conditional-assumption requirement; MOCK-2 refuses every failed mock identity proof; mock/config/hook incremental steps; failure categories in runtime expectations; two loose rejection assertions tightened (old pins kept in superseded_pins).

superseded_incremental_sequences.meaning: Apply the steps in order to a copy of base_dir. After every step, the incremental-update answer for the importer's claim must equal a cold rebuild of the same snapshot, with no stale target. runtime_expect is what node --test does on that snapshot.

steps.why: exporter mutation: target reassigns its live binding (R-BIND-2); the test's 'app.target' assertion fails at runtime
import edit to an extensionless specifier (E3-X1); Node cannot resolve it
target deleted: no target, and no stale NodeId may remain

superseded_incremental_sequences.reason: correction 2: added mock/config/hook steps; runtime failures are now categorized

incremental_sequences.meaning: Apply the steps in order to a copy of base_dir. After every step: (1) the incremental-update answer for the importer's claim equals expected_class AND equals a cold rebuild of the same snapshot; (2) no claim names a deleted or replaced NodeId; (3) node --test with node_args on the snapshot gives runtime_expect, where a failure must show the stated error category.
